My reason for the foundation to care about him is that he has anxiety, so it could be bad for the foundation to have an anomaly that is depressive.

Why? This is a dude stuck in a walkie talkie, they can just, lock him in a faraday cage and forget about him.

Also, they discover that because of his situation, he could be some kind of shield from the visual memetic effect such as SCP 12 for example.

What I really want to know is 'when you write this as a SCP article, what are the big plots beats and how are you getting from a to b to c to the ending'.

item.title: Re: Trapped in the walkie-talkie (Search greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
I have very mixed feelings on this. On the one hand, I can totally see there being this really nice, emotional arc as the Agent trapped in the walkie-talkie like, grows as a person and learns to overcome their flaws and gradually put his old team back together and stuff; on the other, I'm not exactly sure what your plan for executing on this is?

How are you planning on telling this story? Via interview logs? Or the journal entries entirely? Why are the Foundation so willing to go along with this? It seems to me that there's some major issues with him actually doing this so like, what do the Foundation actually like, get him to do?

I kinda wonder about whether this would work as a tale: the actual narrative is extremely focussed on the SCPs growth and that usually implies to me that a story written from the perspective of the SCP would be more effective than a SCP article solely because it's easier to get into the head of the SCP that way.

item.title: Re: Trapped in the walkie-talkie (Search greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
It will use the █

So, not a big fan of hiding the origin of this anomaly behind a black box. Why not go a bit into these traumatic events that cost the lives of their teammates and trapped them in the walkie talkie?

before he was trapped in the walkie-talkie, he has anxiety issues, such as a fear of skip and all that. But now he's more confident because he can more focus on what he hears.

This seems like a HUGE leap. His anxiety is just gone because he's trapped in a walkie talkie and "can focus" better on the spoken word? I don't know if I buy that would negate long term anxiety issues.

I'm missing the progression of the plot here… what is the arc?

item.title: Re: Trapped in the walkie-talkie (Search greenlights)
Re: Trapped in the walkie-talkie (Search greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Responding to IRC chat request.

I'm not sure how I feel about this. I think there is some potential to play with the character here. A walkie-talkie implies a few things, like someone on the other end and the exchange of signals. If it's just an MTF member stuck in a walkie-talkie, that could be fine. It's distressing after all, especially if they have a goal like leading their MTF.

And I think that might be where the snag is from me. There's a weird disconnect of someone that "gets over their anxiety" and decides to reform their team, mostly because anxiety isn't something that is easily gotten over without years of work, and even then that's just to cope with it. But I have some doubts that the Foundation would allow a former MTF who is essentially compromised go back to leading a team, especially given how limited their scope of expertise is in their present state.

I'm conflicted. I think there could be some potential here, but the idea as a whole just isn't really appealing to me too strongly. Regardless, I think I'll offer a tentative greenlight, because I think it might be more of a disagreement on my part with some headcanon stuff rather than a concept I don't approve of.

item.title: Re: Trapped in the walkie-talkie (Search greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Hi Bawower! I'm here to give you a crit-

nitpicket
notpocket

I find the concept to be intriguing. An MTF trapped in a walkie-talkie? Cool!

Although, there isn't a lot of narrative described here in the idea post.

Agent Joly was an MTF that has made contact with an SCP.

Was the SCP the walkie-talkies? Was it an unrelated SCP?

-has major anxiety and when he cannot control himself, he will shout really loudly on all walkie-talkies.

Why is this important for the narrative you are trying to tell? Writing a character with mental health concerns is difficult- and should be approached with nuance.

This SCP is depressive and because of his depression, it can make a lot of damage.

Your hook is actually "MTF trapped in a walkie-talkie".

"-it can make a lot of damage" I caution you to avoid this as a plotline- unless you have a really good reason to do so- I highly recommend you avoid it.

I hope this helps! Thank you for sharing this!

item.title: Trapped in the walkie-talkie (Search greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama

Elevator Pitch: So a guy is trapped inside of a walkie-talkie. He was an MTF but has made contact with an SCP. He can talk in the walkie-talkie and to the ones on the same channel.

Central Narrative: Agent Joly was an MTF that has made contact with an SCP (It will use the █). So now is trapped inside and his comrades are all dead. So, before he was trapped in the walkie-talkie, he has anxiety issues, such as a fear of skip and all that. But now he's more confident because he can't be hurt in his state. So the foundation will give him some kind of secretary to help him to do some stuff. He will have a recording device that will act as some kind of journal. The journal was brought to him because the foundation wanted to record his progression. In the end, when he's going to discover that he's more confident, he will reform his mobile task force.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: MTF trapped in a walkie-talkie.
